cim: Latin America Makes Progress in Data Governance for Ethical and Inclusive Artificial Intelligence
cim_eredeti: Latin America Makes Progress in Data Governance for Ethical and Inclusive Artificial Intelligence
szoveg_eredeti:
Data governance is essential to ensuring that digital transformation and the development of artificial intelligence (AI) are carried out responsibly, inclusively and in a manner that respects human rights. Its importance lies in establishing clear rules and responsibilities regarding how data is collected, used, protected and shared, as well as who can access it and under what conditions. To this end, UNESCO promotes practical tools to help governments and regulatory authorities strengthen data management, protection and sharing.

One year after the launch of the Data Governance Toolkit: Navigating the Data in the Digital Age, the initiative is expanding its reach across Latin America and the Caribbean with the publication of its Spanish-language edition. The document provides practical guidance for developing inclusive data governance frameworks that are equipped to address the challenges of artificial intelligence.

The Toolkit, launched on 8 July 2025, is the result of the work of the Broadband Commission for Sustainable Development, led by UNESCO in collaboration with the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) and the African Union Commission, with the participation of institutions and experts.

By helping governments establish robust frameworks for data access, protection, sharing and stewardship, the Toolkit contributes to achieving the objectives of the Roadmap for Ethical Artificial Intelligence in Latin America and the Caribbean 2026–2027 and building the data ecosystems the region needs to develop and govern AI responsibly. It also complements other regional initiatives, such as the Caribbean Artificial Intelligence Policy Roadmap.

In Peru, these advances in data governance are part of an ongoing effort to strengthen public policies for the responsible development and use of artificial intelligence. In 2026, the country published its National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2026–2030, whose situational analysis incorporated UNESCO's Artificial Intelligence Readiness Assessment (RAM), conducted in 2025, as an input.

Meanwhile, the Regulations of the AI Law (No. 31814), approved in 2025, establish specific provisions on the ethical use of AI, transparency, human oversight and personal data protection. Furthermore, under the framework of its Fifth Complementary Provision, Peru published its National Data Governance Strategy 2026–2030 in 2026, together with a Data Governance Action Plan to guide its implementation.

The dissemination of the Toolkit is complemented by training opportunities for public officials and staff from regulatory bodies. The course Data Governance for Inclusive Digital & AI Futures, jointly promoted by UNESCO and UNDP, received more than 1,000 applications across its first two cohorts in 2026. Of these applications, 84% came from government and regulatory body personnel. The second cohort brought together participants from 22 countries across Latin America and the Caribbean, including Peru.

This participation helps expand opportunities for regional exchange and learning on the frameworks and capacities needed to ensure responsible data governance.

In addition to the Toolkit and training courses, UNESCO and The GovLab have developed an interactive self-assessment tool that enables institutions to examine their data governance practices and identify opportunities to apply the guidance provided in the document.

UNESCO is also working with its partners on new initiatives that link data governance with linguistic diversity and the rights of Indigenous Peoples. In this area, the Organization supports the Indigenous Language Data Commons Incubator, a six-month initiative that supports Indigenous-led teams in developing fundable, community-governed data ecosystems that serve Indigenous and minority languages.

The call for applications received more than 180 submissions from over 50 countries, and the selection process is currently underway.

Strengthening data governance is not merely a technical matter; it also involves establishing the conditions for digital transformation and artificial intelligence to contribute to sustainable development, protect human rights, and address the needs of societies in their diverse contexts. For countries such as Peru, these tools provide guidance for developing institutional frameworks that enable the opportunities offered by technological innovation to be harnessed responsibly.

Discover the upcoming activities and available tools to strengthen institutional capacities in this area.

UNESCO invites its partners to develop tailored guidance for priority sectors, starting with:

→ AI-Ready Data: Building on its work on data governance, UNESCO is developing a new area of work focused on AI-ready data. Its goal is to help Member States govern, assess, improve and maintain the quality of public sector data needed for responsible, inclusive and locally relevant AI applications.

UNESCO and its partners continue to expand the content of the Toolkit and broaden their range of training courses in response to strong demand from governments.

→ In person: 31st International Congress of CLAD, Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic, 18–20 November 2026.

→ Online: UNESCO and UNDP course with instructor support, Data Governance for Inclusive Digital & AI Futures, Cohort 3, first quarter of 2027 (date to be confirmed).

Would you be interested in collaborating with us through regional workshops, online training, technical assistance, sector-specific data governance guidance, or joint initiatives such as the Indigenous Language Data Commons?

This article is related to the United Nation’s Sustainable Development Goals.
